canonical.title: Eat — Sandakan & Sepilok: Where Story Beats Star Count

parent.title: A first-visit guide to Sandakan & Sepilok

siblings.title: Sleep — Sandakan & Sepilok: character stays from jungle lodges to river camps
siblings.summary: Where to base a first Borneo trip: Sepilok jungle lodges, Kinabatangan river camps, a turtle-island chalet and Sandakan heritage town stays — chosen for character, not category.

siblings.title: Do — Sandakan & Sepilok: wildlife, river, caves & history
siblings.summary: The accessible, semi-adventurous Sandakan/Sepilok playbook: Sepilok wildlife trio, the Kinabatangan cruise, caves, turtles and the town WWII history.

siblings.title: See — Sandakan & Sepilok: heritage icons, wildlife & coast
siblings.summary: What to see in and around Sandakan & Sepilok — the colonial Heritage Trail, the Death March memorial, Sepilok wildlife icons, and the wild Kinabatangan.

siblings.title: Offbeat Sandakan & Sepilok: ghosts, croquet, cow-dung tarts & a 2-million-bat exodus
siblings.summary: The quirky layer of Sandakan & Sepilok — bombed-flat Little Hong Kong, a leper-island POW escape, a colonial croquet lawn, cow-dung-shaped tarts, and natural oddities.

siblings.title: Culture in Sandakan & Sepilok: museums, temples, markets & festivals (with dates)
siblings.summary: Sandakan colonial-port culture decoded: museums, Chinese temples, the war memorial, water-village markets and a full festival calendar with 2026 dates.

siblings.title: Around & day-trips: Sandakan & Sepilok logistics
siblings.summary: Practical hops in, out and around Sandakan/Sepilok plus a costed day-trip orbit for a first Borneo visit.

sources.title: https://www.mysabah.com/wordpress/ufo-tart-of-sandakan/
sources.claim: UFO tart origin (1955 Hainanese baker Fu Ah On, accidental over-baking), price ~RM2.50, kopitiams that sell it, and Sabah's 5 May 'UFO Tart Day'.

sources.title: https://www.traveloka.com/en-sg/explore/activities/top-5-must-try-eats-in-sandakan-sabah/48440
sources.claim: UFO tart description and San Da Gen location; English Tea House scone/tea; Yap Syn Kee grass jelly; Ngee Lee coconut pudding in a shell.

sources.title: https://www.mysabah.com/wordpress/sandakan-food-at-sim-sim-water-village/
sources.claim: Sim Sim Water Village eating: Bridges 7 and 8, Kau Kee G68 spring noodle and century-egg dumpling (sells out before 10am), Sim-Sim 88 seafood hours, no-MSG claim.

sources.title: https://www.englishteahouse.org/sandakan_agnes_keith.html
sources.claim: English Tea House sits in restored colonial Newlands beside Agnes Newton Keith's home, with sprawling lawns over Sandakan Bay; fine-dining western cuisine.

sources.title: https://www.sepilokforestedgeresort.com/eat-drink
sources.claim: The Nest at Sepilok Forest Edge: Bornean Contemporary cuisine, signature dishes and prices (asam pedas oxtail RM63, hinava RM36, lamb curry RM48, nasi lemak burger RM31), 7am-10pm.

sources.title: https://sabahtourism.com/article/sandakan-little-hong-kong-of-north-borneo/
sources.claim: Sandakan became the 'Little Hong Kong' of Sabah by the 1930s via pre-WWII Cantonese merchant immigration.

sources.title: https://sabahguide.com/ethnic-groups/chinese-sabah/
sources.claim: Hainanese founded Sandakan's kopitiam culture; Hakka is the Chinese community's internal lingua franca; Sabah Chinese food blends Hakka/Cantonese/Hokkien.

sources.title: https://medium.com/@sixtybolts/your-definitive-guide-to-sabah-noodle-dishes-be9466fb04a9
sources.claim: Sandakan spring noodles (Hong Kong diaspora, 'rubber noodles') and fish-paste noodles served clear/curry/prawn or Hakka style with minced pork.

sources.title: https://www.foodiestravelblog.com/post/top-10-food-in-sandakan
sources.claim: Persatuan Perikanan (fishermen's association) no-menu seafood feast; sang har mee at Empire; Ba Lin rooftop sea view; Kafeteria/Sepilok eats.

sources.title: https://sabaheats.com/guide-food-hunting-sandakan/
sources.claim: Detailed Sandakan food trail with stalls/kopitiams, addresses and specialties (Central Market kueh teow stall, Kong Teck, Wing Hup Lee, Persatuan Perikanan, Pasar Kim Fung).

sources.title: https://milas.travel/top-best-foods-in-sandakan/
sources.claim: Daily food budget RM30-50; night-market meals under RM15; seafood bak kut teh at Nam Chai; ngiu chap; latok sea grapes; salted-fish fried rice.

sources.title: https://clladventureborneo.com/famous-food-in-sandakan/
sources.claim: 15 famous Sandakan dishes incl. hinava (Kadazan-Dusun raw fish), ikan/lokan bakar, kam heong & butter prawns at Empire/Ocean King, kolo mee.

sources.title: https://travelwithlens.com/sandakan-food/
sources.claim: Sim Sim seafood (chef Ah Kit, salted fish), Nam Chai peppery seafood bak kut teh, Gold Crown UFO tart, Empire prawn noodles.

sources.title: https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/wet-market-world-sabahan-chef-230000712.html
sources.claim: Sang nyuk mian definition (Hakka 'raw pork noodle', pork cooked in cloudy broth, served kon lau or soup); Moon n Star among Sandakan's best.

sources.title: https://danielfooddiary.com/2025/11/24/sabahsandakanufotart/
sources.claim: UFO tart is a genuine ~70-year Sabah heritage snack now exported (kaya/matcha flavours sold in Singapore).

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g303997-d2442815-Reviews-Sim_Sim_Seafood_Restaurant-Sandakan_Sandakan_Division_Sabah.html
sources.claim: Sim Sim Seafood Restaurant praised for Sandakan-style ikan bakar (grilled fish half-fried then charcoal-grilled to order).

sources.title: https://www.bilitrainforestlodge.com/pages/buli-sim-sim-water-village
sources.claim: Buli Sim Sim is the original townsite of Sandakan (founded 1879), hundreds of wooden stilt houses on the sea, reachable by plank walkways.

sources.title: https://harbourmallsandakan.com/waterfront-seafood-restaurant/
sources.claim: Waterfront Seafood Bar & Grill at Harbour Mall: open-air dining right by the sea, fresh seafood, white clams and butter prawns.

sources.title: https://wanderlog.com/place/details/2626737/waterfront-seafood-restaurant-bar--grill
sources.claim: Waterfront Seafood reviews highlight white clams, dry butter prawns, generous portions and reasonable prices.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g303997-d17351143-Reviews-Ocean_king_Seafood_Restaurant-Sandakan_Sandakan_Division_Sabah.html
sources.claim: Ocean King Seafood (Batu Sapi): open-air floor over the water with live tanks to pick your own; ranked #5; pricier, value mixed.

sources.title: https://food.malaysiamostwanted.com/venues/ocean-king-seafood-restaurant-sandakan
sources.claim: Ocean King sources seafood locally and serves traditional Chinese seafood preparations.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g303997-d1166938-Reviews-English_Tea_House_Restaurant-Sandakan_Sandakan_Division_Sabah.html
sources.claim: English Tea House reviews: loved for view, lawn and atmosphere; food quality mixed (some inconsistencies noted).

sources.title: https://sabaheats.com/balin-roofgarden-coolest-rooftop-garden-bar-bistro-sandakan/
sources.claim: Ba Lin Roof Garden is Sandakan's only rooftop garden bar-bistro atop NAK Hotel, western menu, bay views.

sources.title: https://www.mysabah.com/wordpress/pasar-malam-kim-fung-night-market/
sources.claim: Kim Fung Night Market: Saturday only 5-10pm, ~6.5km from centre, hundreds of stalls of Chinese and halal street food, lion/fish dance from 8pm, authentic non-touristy.

sources.title: https://evendo.com/locations/malaysia/sandakan/attraction/sandakan-the-little-hong-kong
sources.claim: Sandakan earned the 'Little Hong Kong' nickname 1920s-1950s for its thriving Chinese merchant community and shophouse architecture.

sources.title: https://www.sepilokjungleresort.com/
sources.claim: Sepilok Jungle Resort (Banana Cafe) is at Jalan Rambutan, Sepilok Mile 14, near the orangutan sanctuary.

sources.title: https://kafeteria-sepilok.placejoys.com/
sources.claim: Kafeteria Sepilok, steps from the Orangutan Centre: sandwiches from RM6, rice/noodles from RM8, cold coffee RM2.80, daily 8-4, cash only.

sources.title: https://www.sandspice.com/sepilok-borneo/
sources.claim: Sepilok dining is very limited and pricey; Sepilok Nature Lodge restaurant ~RM98 for two with beer, western-leaning; Banana Cafe weak.

sources.title: https://www.travelfish.org/eatandmeet/malaysia/sabah/sabah/sandakan/eat
sources.claim: The Nest has the most interesting menu in the whole Sandakan area; Kafeteria Sepilok and Banana Cafe are the budget local options near the sanctuary.

sources.title: https://www.naturalworldsafaris.com/asia/borneo/safaris-and-planning/where-to-stay-in-borneo/sepilok-nature-resort
sources.claim: Sepilok Nature Resort: cooked-to-order breakfast, all-day deli, east-west fusion served on a terrace over the lodge lake/forest.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotel_Review-g1137932-d655181-Reviews-Kinabatangan_Riverside_Lodge-Sukau_Kinabatangan_District_Sabah.html
sources.claim: Kinabatangan river lodges serve included, locally-sourced buffet meals; barefoot dining with sarongs and riverside tables at some lodges.

sources.title: https://www.sabahtravel.com/attraction/sabah-traditional-cooking-class
sources.claim: Sabah Traditional Cooking Class (Papar): market tour plus family-home cooking of rendang/likku with 'Mummy Halimah', min 2, book a day ahead.

sources.title: https://www.tyhborneotours.com/Cooking-Class
sources.claim: TYH Borneo Tours offers a Sabahan cooking class experience that can be arranged on request.

sources.title: https://harbourmallsandakan.com/2025/01/08/the-sea-garden-sim-sim/
sources.claim: The Sea Garden Sim-sim is a waterside seafood dining option in the Harbour Mall Sandakan orbit.

sources.title: https://www.theadventuremanual.com/sepilok-travel-guide
sources.claim: Sepilok dining trio: The Lake Bistro (Malay+international, lake views), Banana Cafe (simple jungle fare), The Nest (burgers/wraps/curries, beautiful at night) — Nest often has items missing.

sources.title: https://pureglutton.com/sandakan-food-trail-1
sources.claim: Sandakan food trail: Central Market kueh teow stall since 1940 (one item only), Kong Teck fish noodles, Sim Sim Bridge 7 rubber wantan noodles, Nam Chai seafood bak kut teh, Bun Hock UFO tarts.

sources.title: https://wanderlog.com/place/details/8038822/sandagen-downtown-night-market
sources.claim: Sanda'Gen Downtown Night Market sits on the seawall at Coastal Road (Tembok Bandar Sandakan) with about 36 food stalls.
